claims.text: Current experimental and computational methods have limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency for determining the listed high-temperature and liquid-state properties of high-entropy alloys.
A systematic dataset of experimentally reported high-entropy-alloy microstructures and metallurgy-specific features is available.
The systematic microstructure dataset can be used to support machine-learning-based phase classification.
The proposed machine-learning intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys in both high-temperature solid and liquid states across a large compositional space.
Microstructure and phase formation act as the structural mediator for the proposed predictions.
Machine learning can extract useful insights and trends from documented high-entropy-alloy microstructures, processing information, and metallurgy-specific features.
The extracted trends enable prediction of melting temperature.
The extracted trends enable prediction of enthalpy of fusion.
The extracted trends enable prediction of entropy of fusion.
The extracted trends enable prediction of volume change upon melting.
The extracted trends enable prediction of liquid thermodynamic properties.
The intervention will improve predictive accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve the availability of the listed thermophysical-property determinations.
The intervention will improve the efficiency of the listed thermophysical-property determinations.
The intervention is limited to high-entropy alloys in their high-temperature solid and liquid states.
The accuracy of the machine-learning approach depends on the quality and completeness of the documented microstructure and metallurgy data.
